messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: streaming.decode p99 spike detected across us-west-2 tuft-rt cluster. p95 also bumped. Auto-runbooks triggered.
ops-bot: Incident severity: S2. Estimated customer impact: medium (some streaming sessions showing stalls).
sam: Oncall here — looking. Any recent kernel/driver changes rolled to tuft-rt this morning?
mike: We rolled TRT8 + flashattn v2 at 08:10 PT. CI flagged a kernel compile pass at 07:55 that landed a new compilepath flag (ENABLE_COMPILEPATH_OPT).
nina: Confirming deploy-bot shows two deployments: model-serving/trt8:2026-03-14 and runtime/kernel:compilepath-2026-03-14a.
sam: Good catch. Correlating metrics now. Which machines are showing the worst tail?
alejandra: tail is concentrated on g5dn-16x nodes in tuft-rt pool A. p99 token-latency up ~3.2x for streaming decode. Non-streaming (sync infer) not affected as badly.
mike: That pattern smells like KV-cache/eviction behaviour — compilepath changes touched allocator heuristics.
sam: Reproducing locally with a small streaming harness. Running the same kernel compile (compilepath-2026-03-14a) against a trimmed flashattn workload.
sam: local run shows occasional tail stalls with logs: 
```
[WARN] kv_cache: eviction_threshold reached, pin-fail=0
[DEBUG] compilepath: pagefault fallback path engaged for decode kernel
```
mike: That log matches customer tracer we pulled from tuft-rt. Paging/eviction increased. We should trigger a smoke rollback of the compilepath patch and see if tail drops.
nina: Recommend immediate mitigations: 1) route streaming traffic to tuft-rt-pool-B (older kernel) via smart-routing policy, 2) scale up dedicated warm pools to reduce batching pressure, 3) revert compilepath flag on a small canary.
sam: I can push a routing override. Deploy-bot do you have the routing rollback ready?
deploy-bot: Scheduled action: create route override to direct 30% of tuft-rt streaming to tuft-rt-pool-B. Command ready: `redwood route override --from tuft-rt --to tuft-rt-pool-B --percent 30 --reason "runtime tail mitigation"`
alejandra: Start with 30% then ramp. If we see p99 improve in those sessions, that's strong signal the new kernel/compilepath change is culprit.
mike: Meanwhile I'll stage a compilepath rollback onto canary nodes: `kernel-package install compilepath-2026-03-13` on 3 nodes and run streaming load.
sam: Do we have a quick kill switch if rollback regresses something else?
alejandra: Yes — we have automated rollback and traffic will respect model pinning. If canary fails, we abort using autoscaler to drain.
sam: Doing the route override now. Pasting commands: 
```
# route 30% to older pool
redwood route override --from tuft-rt --to tuft-rt-pool-B --percent 30 --reason "runtime tail mitigation"
redwood monitor metric set --name streaming.decode.p99 --alert-threshold 2.0x --notify-channel eng-oncall
```
ops-bot: Action logged: route override initiated by sam.
(5m later)
sam: Route override active. Initial telemetry: p99 for sessions routed to pool-B is down ~45% vs baseline. Overall cluster p99 improved ~18%.
alejandra: Can we escalate routing to 60% while we validate canary rollback? That should reduce customer impact further.
mike: Canary rollback applied to 3 nodes and running 100 concurrent streams. Observed tail stalls on canary disappeared in the load harness.
sam: Ramp to 60% now.
ops-bot: Action logged: route override updated to 60% by sam.
(10m later)
nina: p99 dropped near-normal on most metrics. Customer impact appears mitigated. Need postmortem coverage: root cause looks like compilepath allocator tweak interacting with flashattn kernel paging behavior under streaming KV cache patterns.
mike: Proposed next steps: 1) revert compilepath change cluster-wide (schedule), 2) add a targeted canary test in CI simulating long-running streaming KV-cache workloads, 3) add a runtime guard to avoid eviction churn when compilepath flag is present.
sam: I'll open an incident ticket and assign owners. Quick notes for ticket: timestamps, affected pools, mitigation (route override -> 60%), canary rollback success, metrics snapshots.
alejandra: Also ping customer-success for any high-volume customers in tuft-rt pool A — they may have experienced stalls.
nina: I'll draft an internal blameless postmortem and tag eng-runtime + eng-sre. Add regression alert for compilepath merges touching allocator heuristics.
sam: Thanks team. Keeping the channel open for 1 hour for additional telemetry checks, then we'll close and move to postmortem thread. :white_check_mark:
